newsitem.title: CANADA: Anvil in loan for Faro stripping program.
newsitem.headline: Anvil in loan for Faro stripping program.

text.p: Anvil Range Mining Corp said on Monday that it agreed in principle with 27.7 percent owner Cominco Ltd for a C$15 million secured loan to fund a stripping program at its Grum ore deposit in Faro, Yukon.

The lead and zinc miner said finalization of the loan was subject to a due diligence review, completion of documentation and regulatory approval. Anvil Range said its major shareholders were also discussing up to C$5 million of additional funding on the same terms.

"The stripping program is necessary to prepare the mine for the resumption of full scale operations and will take between three and four months to complete," said Anvil Range Chief Executive Patrick Mars.

The mine was temporarily shut down last December because of lower than expected base metal prices, a strong Canadian dollar and delays in stripping the mine. The mill operation was suspended earlier this year.
Anvil Range shares were untraded on the day, but closed on Friday at C$2.95 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

The loan would be fully secured by all of assets of the company and carry an interest rate of 8.5 percent, with final repayment to be made by October 17, 2001 or earlier at the option of Cominco if Anvil Range raised more than C$20 million in new equity.

In conjunction with the loan, Anvil said it would also issue 5 million warrants to Cominco exercisable at C$3 a share, for a term of the earlier of three years or 1.5 years after final repayment of the loan.

Anvil said it would seek to raise between C$20 million and C$30 million in equity to fund additional capital equipment and provide working capital, either by way of a rights offering, public offering or private placement.
It said Cominco Ltd confirmed that subject to market conditions it would participate in its pro-rata share in any such equity issue.
The Grum, Vangorda and Dy deposits at Faro have proven and probable reserves of 45.8 million tonnes grading 8.34 percent zinc and lead, 52.6 grams per tonne of silver and 0.70 gram per tonne gold.
